title: Thomson Reuters Completes Acquisition of Casetext, Inc.
author: Thomson Reuters

kp.k: Thomson Reuters acquires Casetext for $650 million cash
kp.d: The corporate press release reports that Thomson Reuters completed its previously announced acquisition of legal-technology provider Casetext on August 17, 2023, for $650 million in cash. It presents the acquisition as part of its strategy to bring generative AI solutions to customers.
qs: TORONTO, August 17, 2023 – Thomson Reuters Corporation (“Thomson Reuters”) (NYSE / TSX: TRI) announced today that it has closed on its previously announced acquisition of Casetext, Inc. (“Casetext”), a provider of technology for legal professionals, for a purchase price of $650 million in cash.

The acquisition supports Thomson Reuters ‘build, partner and buy’ strategy to bring generative AI solutions to its customers and the company's efforts to redefine the future of professionals through applications of generative AI.

kp.k: CoCounsel targets research, review, deposition preparation and contract analysis
kp.d: The release reports that Casetext serves more than 10,000 law firms and corporate legal departments and describes its GPT-4-powered CoCounsel assistant as delivering several legal tasks in minutes. Claims of greater efficiency and higher-quality representation are corporate product claims, rather than findings from a reported performance study.
qs: Founded in 2013, Casetext uses advanced AI and machine learning to build technology for legal professionals, creating solutions that help them work more efficiently and provide higher-quality representation to more clients.
Casetext’s customers include more than 10,000 law firms and corporate legal departments.
Its key products include CoCounsel, an AI legal assistant powered by GPT-4 that delivers document review, legal research memos, deposition preparation, and contract analysis in minutes.

kp.k: AI expansion combines investment, Microsoft collaboration and Westlaw pilots
kp.d: Thomson Reuters reports a commitment to invest $100 million-plus annually in AI integration across flagship content and technology products. It also describes collaboration with Microsoft on a Microsoft 365 Copilot plugin and a legal drafting solution using Westlaw, Practical Law and Document Intelligence, alongside a July beta launch of generative AI capabilities in Westlaw for select customers.
qs: Other recent developments include Thomson Reuters commitment to invest $100 million-plus annually to integrate AI into its flagship content and technology solutions, as well as its work with Microsoft for a new plugin with Microsoft 365 Copilot, with the two companies collaborating on a legal drafting solution that leverages Westlaw, Practical Law and Document Intelligence.
In July, Thomson Reuters also launched a beta program to pilot new generative AI capabilities in Westlaw with select customers.

kp.k: Executives anticipate transformed work, productivity and access to justice
kp.d: Thomson Reuters CEO Steve Hasker predicts that the combined businesses will accelerate generative AI breakthroughs and revolutionize professionals' work. Casetext CEO Jake Heller presents the acquisition as an opportunity to scale its vision and pursue greater productivity, more impactful work and increased access to justice. These are attributed executive expectations, not demonstrated outcomes.
qs: “Together, we will accelerate breakthroughs in generative AI for the benefit of our customers and markets. We believe this will revolutionize the way professionals work, and the work that they do.”

“Joining Thomson Reuters provides us with an unparalleled opportunity to scale the Casetext vision and accelerate breakthroughs for legal professionals. As we look to unlock generative AI’s full potential to drive greater productivity, more impactful work and increased access to justice, there could not be a better home for our brand, talent and products.”

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Thomson Reuters claims that Casetext's AI improves legal professionals' efficiency, representation quality and capacity, and that CoCounsel performs specified legal tasks in minutes.
pts.d: The corporate release describes these as existing capabilities. It identifies CoCounsel as a GPT-4-powered legal assistant supporting document review, legal research memo preparation, deposition preparation and contract analysis. It does not claim that the tool replaces lawyers or operates without human supervision.

pts.k: Steve Hasker predicts accelerated generative-AI breakthroughs and a transformation of both how professionals work and what work they do.
pts.d: Thomson Reuters president and CEO Steve Hasker links this prediction to combining Thomson Reuters and Casetext. His statement concerns professionals and customer markets broadly rather than specifying particular legal roles, staffing changes or pricing effects.

pts.k: Jake Heller presents the acquisition as an opportunity to scale legal AI and pursue greater productivity, more impactful work and increased access to justice.
pts.d: Casetext CEO Jake Heller frames these outcomes as the potential of generative AI to be unlocked through joining Thomson Reuters, not as measured outcomes already achieved. The access-to-justice aspiration is not accompanied by a specified beneficiary population or delivery mechanism.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The release offers product descriptions, customer reach, investment and integration activity, and executive assertions rather than outcome studies or benchmarks.
pts.d: Thomson Reuters reports more than 10,000 law-firm and corporate-legal-department customers, a completed $650 million cash acquisition, an annual AI investment commitment exceeding $100 million, Microsoft collaboration and a Westlaw beta program. These establish reported commercial reach and development activity, not measured improvements in speed, quality or access to justice. Hasker also invokes the company's acquisition and innovation track record. No task-testing methodology, comparative baseline, quality assessment or access-to-justice data is supplied.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: Current capability claims are made as of August 17, 2023; broader transformation predictions have no deadline and are linked to post-acquisition scaling and continued development.
pts.d: The release presents CoCounsel's task delivery 'in minutes' as a current capability without specifying task complexity or operating conditions. It reports a July 2023 Westlaw pilot limited to select customers and an annual investment commitment. Hasker's transformation prediction is expressly framed as a belief, while Heller describes potential still to be unlocked. Neither supplies a timetable for profession-wide transformation or increased access to justice.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The claimed beneficiaries are legal professionals, law firms, corporate legal departments and their clients, with broader aspirations for professional markets and access to justice.
pts.d: Legal professionals are expected to perform tasks faster and undertake more impactful work; clients are said to benefit from higher-quality representation and professionals' ability to serve more people. Law firms and corporate legal departments are identified as existing customers, without segmentation by size or practice area. Hasker's prediction extends to Thomson Reuters' professional customers and markets more generally. Heller invokes access to justice but does not identify which underserved groups would gain legal help. Casetext is described as a technology provider, not as an alternative legal service provider delivering legal work.
